target_customer: Multifamily commercial real estate acquisition teams and investors that screen many deals
problem: Acquisition teams spend analyst time reading offering memorandums, rent rolls and T-12s to screen deals that do not match their buying criteria; Cresa automated the screening and first-pass diligence.
business_model: B2B SaaS for CRE acquisition teams (pricing not stated), with a free rent comp research tool as lead generation
product_category: AI deal screening and underwriting automation for commercial real estate

founders.name: Teddy Li
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder and CEO but with no bio, and the same page shows a Former Founders heading above his profile; the launch post names only Weeks and Kwadwo.

founders.name: Weeks Mensah
previous_startups: Managing director of the first PPP coworking and incubator space in Queens, NY (unnamed)
founders.background_notes: YC page: product and finance professional and CRE investor; the launch post says he and Kwadwo are second-time YC founders.

founders.name: Kwadwo Nyarko
founders.background_notes: YC page: lead engineer at WeWork building a procurement system; born in Ghana, raised in the Bronx.

competitors.name: Skyline AI
competitors.what: AI platform for commercial real estate investment analysis using data from many sources

competitors.name: SeeCares
competitors.what: AI underwriting tools for commercial real estate lending and deals
competitors.traction_then: Reported 1.2 billion dollars of deals closed since April 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting figures from messy PDFs such as rent rolls and OMs and syncing them to acquisition models needed document parsing and later fine-tuned multimodal models; hard parts but within reach of a small technical team.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow integration with a team's own acquisition model gives some stickiness, but the model and document parsing approach could be copied by larger CRE data vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent buying or copying Nophin; later AI underwriting startups raised larger rounds (CarbonAI in 2026, Henry AI in 2025).

market_need_then: The launch post says the founders built an end to end underwriting tool first and learned that screening deals outside buying criteria wastes analyst time. A 2021 article shows demand for AI underwriting in CRE (SeeCares reported 1.2 billion dollars in deals).

branding.domain_note: Company site nophin.com now redirects to the YC company page; the product ran on cresa.nophin.com (sub-domain), and Cresa is also the name of a large unrelated brokerage.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Product led and plain: AI analyst for CRE deal screening

branding.brand_signature: The product name Cresa for the AI analyst

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; the product name Cresa collides with an established brokerage called Cresa, which swamps search results.

outcome_analysis: Nophin joined YC Winter 2022 with experienced second time founders and, per one database, a 2 million dollar seed in April 2022 backed by Goodwater, Liquid 2 and MetaProp. The cause of the inactive status is not public: no shutdown, acquisition or pivot report was found, and the website now redirects to the YC page. The product name Cresa collides with a major brokerage of the same name, a plausible but unproven brand cost, so that failure factor is tentative.
notes: Seed of 2.0M in 2022-04 rests on a single database (VCBacked, last updated 2022-04-04); CB Insights lists only 500K total with Liquid 2 Ventures and YC, a conflict. No press release found. Cause of inactive status is not public; the brand_confusion failure factor is a tentative reading. Skyline AI source is a 2018 post and gives no funding; Skyline AI is listed because it predated the batch. Website redirected to the YC page (302) so it is treated as dead.
